newsitem.title: UK: Reed tumbles amid downgrade talk.
newsitem.headline: Reed tumbles amid downgrade talk.

text.p: Shares in Reed International Plc plummeted from their earlier highs amid talk of downgrades following the company's meeting with analysts after today's trading statement, traders said.
The stock was down 49p at 11.01 stg by 1511 GMT after earlier trading as high as 11.89 stg.
Market sources said HSBC James Capel had trimmed earnings estimates for Reed by some seven percent, though analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.
Sources said Salomon analysts had also trimmed forecasts but the analysts declined comment.

Earlier the Anglo-Dutch publisher said it was confident about business prospects for the second half of 1996 and would use strong cash flows to fund acquisitions and invest in its technical infrastructure.
Reed's year-end statement coincided with a presentation on its electronic publshing activities to investors and analysts in London.

The company said its opportunities were substantial in the expanding electronic publishing field and "... with our market-leading franchises, the depth and quality of our content and our considerable technology competencies we are positioned strongly to take full advantage..."
Trading volume in the stock reached an active 9.1 million shares by 1528 GMT.
